problem: A particle $P$ is moving along the curve $y=4{x}^{3}+16x$ such that the $x$-coordinate of $P$ is changing at the rate of $-\frac{1}{4}\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.$ Find the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate when $x=3\,\text{cm}.$

feedback.problem:
A particle $P$ is moving along the curve $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+{x}^{2}$ such that the $x$-coordinate of $P$ is changing at the rate of $-4\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.$ Find the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate when $x=3\,\,\text{cm}.$

$\text{cm}/\text{s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+{x}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+{x}^{2}] \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+{x}^{2}] \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{1}{x+1}+2x).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-4\,\text{cm}/\text{s}$ and $x=3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-4\cdot (\frac{1}{3+1}+2(3)) \\  & =-4\cdot (\frac{1}{4}+6) \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{25}{4} \\  & =-25.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $y$-coordinate is changing at the rate of $-25\text{ }\text{cm}/\text{s}.$
